metadata.description: Stylized major oil provinces/fields for isolated 'lake' visualization. Polygon size roughly reflects relative reserves; shapes are illustrative, not exact reservoir boundaries.
metadata.important_note: These polygons are simplified visual metaphors for education. They are not survey-grade field outlines.

properties.name: Ghawar Field
properties.reserves_note: Remaining proven liquids ~48 bn bbl (Aramco disclosures); ultimate recovery estimates much higher
properties.summary: The world’s largest conventional oil field – a long, narrow structure that has supplied a large share of Saudi production for decades.
properties.description: Ghawar stretches roughly 280 km north–south. It is the classic ‘supergiant’ and the natural centrepiece of any global oil-field view. Production is operated by Saudi Aramco.

aha_moment.title: The giant under the desert
aha_moment.explanation: One single field has produced more oil than most countries ever will. Its remaining reserves are still among the largest of any conventional field.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: A noticeable share of globally traded crude – and therefore of fuels and plastics – has at some point come from this one structure.

properties.name: Orinoco Oil Belt
properties.reserves_note: Major part of Venezuela’s ~304 bn bbl proven reserves; extra-heavy oil
properties.summary: The largest oil accumulation on Earth by reserves – mostly extra-heavy oil that requires special processing.
properties.description: The Orinoco Belt holds the bulk of Venezuela’s world-leading reserves. The oil is extra-heavy; production and exports have been constrained by technology, politics and infrastructure.

aha_moment.title: Biggest reserves, not biggest producer
aha_moment.explanation: Venezuela sits on more proven oil than Saudi Arabia, but most of it is heavy and harder to produce. Reserves ≠ current flow.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: When Venezuelan exports rise or fall, it mainly affects specific heavy-crude refineries rather than every petrol station overnight.

properties.name: Athabasca Oil Sands
properties.reserves_note: Dominant share of Canada’s oil-sands reserves (~163–170 bn bbl total Canadian proven incl. sands)
properties.summary: One of the world’s largest hydrocarbon deposits – bitumen in sand that is mined or produced with steam.
properties.description: The Athabasca oil sands are the reason Canada ranks among the top reserve holders. Extraction is energy-intensive and land-intensive compared with conventional fields.

aha_moment.title: Oil you can dig
aha_moment.explanation: Part of this resource is produced by surface mining – more like a quarry than a classic drill-and-pump field.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Canadian oil sands crude is an important feedstock for refineries in the US Midwest and beyond.

properties.name: Greater Burgan Field
properties.reserves_note: Often cited among the top 2–3 conventional fields historically
properties.summary: Kuwait’s supergiant – historically one of the very largest conventional oil fields.
properties.description: Greater Burgan has been a cornerstone of Kuwaiti production for decades and remains one of the most important single fields globally.

aha_moment.title: Small country, giant field
aha_moment.explanation: A large share of Kuwait’s wealth and export capacity sits in this one cluster of structures.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Burgan-grade crude has long been a staple in global seaborne oil trade.

properties.name: Upper Zakum Field
properties.reserves_note: One of the largest offshore oil fields in the world
properties.summary: A giant offshore field in the Persian Gulf and a pillar of UAE production growth.
properties.description: Upper Zakum is developed with artificial islands and advanced recovery techniques. It is central to Abu Dhabi’s long-term output plans.

aha_moment.title: Oil from the seabed
aha_moment.explanation: Some of the world’s largest remaining conventional reserves sit under shallow Gulf waters, produced from man-made islands and platforms.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: UAE crude is a major component of seaborne supply to Asia and Europe.

properties.name: Rumaila Field
properties.reserves_note: One of Iraq’s most productive fields; remaining reserves still very large in global comparison
properties.summary: Iraq’s flagship southern oil field and one of the most productive single fields worldwide.
properties.description: Rumaila has been a mainstay of Iraqi exports. Together with nearby southern fields it anchors the country’s role in OPEC supply.

aha_moment.title: Iraq’s production engine
aha_moment.explanation: A handful of southern Iraqi fields, led by Rumaila, account for a large share of the country’s oil exports.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Iraqi barrels are an important flexible source in the global market.

properties.name: Safaniya Field
properties.reserves_note: Often described as the world’s largest offshore oil field
properties.summary: The world’s largest offshore conventional oil field.
properties.description: Safaniya has been a key Saudi offshore producer for decades and remains strategically important for medium-grade crude supply.

aha_moment.title: The largest field at sea
aha_moment.explanation: Not all supergiants are under desert – Safaniya shows how much oil sits under the Gulf.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: Offshore Saudi grades are a regular part of long-haul crude trade.

properties.name: Permian Basin
properties.region: West Texas & SE New Mexico, USA
properties.reserves_note: Reserves estimates vary; the basin is currently one of the highest-producing oil provinces in the world
properties.summary: The engine of the modern US shale boom – not the largest by classic reserves, but among the most productive.
properties.description: The Permian produces more oil than most entire countries. Tight-oil drilling transformed it into a swing supplier for global markets.

aha_moment.title: Reserves vs. flow
aha_moment.explanation: The Permian is smaller on a pure reserves map than Orinoco or Ghawar, yet it can out-produce many larger-reserve countries.
aha_moment.everyday_impact: US export growth in the last decade is tightly linked to this one basin.
